summary: Albert Debrunner was a linguist and Indologist. He held academic posts at the universities of Zurich (circa 1903–1907), Basel (circa 1918–1920), Greifswald (circa 1920–1925), Jena (circa 1925–1935), and Bern (circa 1940–1954).

Albert Grünwedel worked in Indology, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (circa 1876–1883) and served as Direktor at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin from circa 1883 to 1921.

Albert Hoefer worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a professor at the University of Greifswald from circa 1840 to 1883 and founded the Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache in 1845.

Albert Thumb was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Freiburg (circa 1884–1888). He later held posts at the University of Freiburg (circa 1893–1909) and the University of Marburg (circa 1909).

Albert Welter specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After earning his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara, he held posts at the University of Winnipeg (circa 1995–2014) and the University of Arizona (circa 2014).

Albion Moonlight Butters works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and also studied at Harvard University and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies under various teachers.

Albrecht Hanisch is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctoral degree at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn. He served as Acting Director of the Nepal Research Centre and Local Representative for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Albrecht Weber was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin under scholars including Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Christian Lassen. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (1848–1901) and the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

Albrecht Wezler was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen under Paul Thieme. He served as Director at the University of Hamburg (attested 1982–2009) and Director General of the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1982–2002).

Aleix Ruiz-Falqués works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs and has held posts at Shan State Buddhist University and Singapore University of Technology and Design.

Alessandro Graheli specializes in Indology and philosophy. Attested in 2022, his appointments include university assistant at the University of Vienna and principal investigator at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
Alex McKay works in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London in 1995 and held a research fellowship at University College London.

Alex Watson works in Indology and philosophy, having studied at Oxford and SOAS, supervised by Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson. His posts include Preceptor at Harvard, Junior Research Fellow at Wolfson College, Oxford, and Professor at Ashoka University.

Alex Wayman was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at UC Berkeley under Ferdinand Diederich Lessing. He held positions at Wisconsin-Madison (circa 1961–1967) and Columbia University (1966–1991).

Alexander Berzin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard University (circa 1967–1972), as well as under traditional teachers including Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche and Ling Rinpoche.

Alexander Coburn Soper worked in history and archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Hamilton College and Princeton University, later holding posts at Bryn Mawr College (circa 1939–1960) and New York University (circa 1960–1980).

Alexander Csoma de Kőrös was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (1816–1818) and under traditional teachers, later serving as sub-librarian at the Asiatic Society from circa 1837 to 1842.

Alexander Gardner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. and Robert H. Sharf, and held a post at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.
Alexander James O'Neill specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He pursued PhD studies at the University of Toronto and held a position as a research fellow at Taisho University.

Alexander Johnston worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served on the Executive Council of Ceylon as chief justice and first member (circa 1811–1819) and was Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (circa 1823–1849).
